questions.scenario: You are creating a container in Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL to store product descriptions with embeddings that have 1,536 dimensions. The container will hold about 3 million items, and searches must have the lowest possible latency and RU cost.
questions.question: Which vector index type should you configure?

options.text: flat
options.why: The flat index supports at most 505 dimensions and performs a brute-force search.

options.text: diskANN
options.why: Correct. diskANN supports up to 4,096 dimensions and provides fast approximate search with low RU cost on large data sets.

options.text: quantizedFlat
options.why: quantizedFlat supports 1,536 dimensions but is a brute-force search that is recommended for about 50,000 vectors or fewer in scope.

options.text: range
options.why: A range index supports equality and range filters, not vector similarity search.

questions.explanation: For millions of high-dimensional vectors, diskANN offers the lowest latency and RU cost.

questions.question: You are defining the vector embedding policy for a container that stores embeddings from text-embedding-3-small. Which THREE properties must you specify for each vector path in the policy?

options.text: path
options.why: Correct. The path identifies the property that contains the vector.

options.text: dimensions
options.why: Correct. dimensions specifies the length of each vector, which is 1536 for text-embedding-3-small.

options.text: distanceFunction
options.why: Correct. distanceFunction specifies the similarity metric, such as cosine.

options.text: partitionKey
options.why: The partition key is a container property and is not part of each vector embedding entry.

options.text: ttl
options.why: Time to live controls item expiration and is not part of the vector embedding policy.

questions.explanation: Each vectorEmbeddings entry describes the path, dataType, dimensions and distanceFunction of the vectors.

questions.question: You need to return the five FAQ items whose embedding property is most similar to a query vector passed as the parameter @q. Which query should you use?

options.text: SELECT TOP 5 c.id, c.question FROM c ORDER BY VectorDistance(c.embedding, @q)
options.why: Correct. ORDER BY VectorDistance returns the most similar items first, and TOP 5 limits the results.

options.text: SELECT c.id, c.question FROM c WHERE c.embedding = @q
options.why: An equality filter finds only identical vectors and does not rank by similarity.

options.text: SELECT c.id, c.question FROM c ORDER BY VectorDistance(c.embedding, @q)
options.why: Without TOP N, the query tries to return many more results, which increases the RU charge and latency.

options.text: SELECT TOP 5 c.id, c.question FROM c WHERE ARRAY_CONTAINS(c.embedding, @q)
options.why: ARRAY_CONTAINS checks whether an array contains a value and does not perform similarity search.

questions.explanation: Vector search uses ORDER BY VectorDistance and should always include a TOP N clause.

questions.question: A container has a vector index on the /embedding path. Inserts have high RU charges and latency. The indexing policy includes the path /* and excludes only /_etag/?. What should you change?

options.text: Remove the vector index from the indexing policy
options.why: Removing the vector index makes searches slower and more expensive and does not address the range index cost.

options.text: Change the distance function from cosine to euclidean
options.why: The distance function does not affect indexing cost on inserts.

options.text: Add /embedding/* to excludedPaths
options.why: Correct. Excluding the vector path from the range index avoids indexing every array element, which lowers insert cost. The vector index still covers the path.

options.text: Change the data type of the vector to float64
options.why: float64 is not a supported data type for the vector policy, and larger values would increase storage.

questions.explanation: Microsoft recommends adding the vector path to excludedPaths so that the range index does not index the vector array.

questions.question: A multitenant retrieval application stores document chunks for many customers in one container that is partitioned by /tenantId. Vector searches must return chunks only from the current customer's documents. What should you do?

options.text: Create a separate vector embedding policy for each tenant
options.why: Policies describe vector paths, not tenants, and do not restrict which items are returned.

options.text: Add WHERE c.tenantId = @tenant to the vector query and scope the query to that partition key value
options.why: Correct. Vector search can be combined with WHERE filters, and the partition key keeps the search inside one tenant's partition.

options.text: Increase the number of dimensions in the vector policy
options.why: The number of dimensions must match the embedding model and does not filter results.

options.text: Filter the results in the application after the query returns the top 100 items
options.why: Filtering afterwards can return too few results for the tenant and still reads other tenants' data.

questions.explanation: Combine ORDER BY VectorDistance with a WHERE filter on tenantId so results come only from the current tenant.
